introduction_markdown:
**General Certificate of Education Board - General Certificate of Education Examination. Further Mathematics 3 (0775), ADVANCED LEVEL, June 2023. Time allowed: two and a half hours.**

Answer ALL questions. For your guidance the approximate mark allocation for parts of each question is indicated in brackets. Mathematical formulae and tables, published by the Board, and noiseless non-programmable electronic calculators are allowed. In calculations, you are advised to show all the steps in your working, giving your answer at each stage.
enonce_intro_markdown: A car of mass $1500\ \mathrm{kg}$ starts from rest and moves along a straight level road surface with its engine working at the rate of $6000v$, where $v$ is the velocity of the car at time $t$. Given that the total resistance to the motion of this car when travelling at speed $v\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$ is $\dfrac{6000v}{u}$ where $u$ is a constant,
incertitudes: Question 4 : le sujet imprime la puissance « 6000 v » sans unité ; elle est prise en watts (v en m/s). La force motrice P/v = 6000 N est alors constante, et c'est ce qui redonne exactement l'équation 4/u = (1/(u - v)) dv/dt demandée en (ii).

questions.enonce_markdown: show that $u$ is the maximum speed of the car along this road,
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Driving force.** The engine works at the rate $P = 6000v$ (in watts), so the driving force is

$$F = \frac{P}{v} = \frac{6000v}{v} = 6000\ \mathrm{N}\quad\text{(constant)}$$

**Equation of motion** along the level road, with resistance $\dfrac{6000v}{u}$:

$$1500\,\frac{dv}{dt} = 6000 - \frac{6000v}{u}$$

**Maximum speed.** The speed cannot increase any more when the acceleration is zero, i.e. when the driving force equals the resistance:

$$6000 = \frac{6000v}{u}\ \Rightarrow\ v = u$$

Moreover $\dfrac{dv}{dt} = 4\left(1 - \dfrac{v}{u}\right)$ is positive for $0 \le v < u$ (the car speeds up) and negative for $v > u$ (it would slow down), so the speed never exceeds $u$ and tends to $u$. Hence $u$ is the maximum (limiting) speed of the car along this road.
themes: motion of a vehicle with resistance

questions.enonce_markdown: show that the equation of motion of this car is $$\frac{4}{u} = \frac{1}{u - v}\frac{dv}{dt}.$$
questions.corrige_markdown:
From part (i), Newton's second law gives

$$1500\,\frac{dv}{dt} = 6000 - \frac{6000v}{u} = \frac{6000(u - v)}{u}$$

Divide both sides by $1500$:

$$\frac{dv}{dt} = \frac{4(u - v)}{u}$$

Divide by $(u - v)$ (non-zero while $v < u$):

$$\frac{1}{u - v}\frac{dv}{dt} = \frac{4}{u}$$

which is the required equation.

questions.enonce_markdown: Hence, find the time taken for the speed of the car to be raised from $0$ to $\tfrac{1}{2}u$.
questions.corrige_markdown:
Separate the variables in $\dfrac{1}{u - v}\dfrac{dv}{dt} = \dfrac{4}{u}$ and integrate from $v = 0$, $t = 0$ to $v = \tfrac{1}{2}u$, $t = T$:

$$\int_0^{u/2}\frac{dv}{u - v} = \frac{4}{u}\int_0^T dt$$

$$\Big[-\ln(u - v)\Big]_0^{u/2} = \frac{4T}{u}$$

$$-\ln\frac{u}{2} + \ln u = \ln 2 = \frac{4T}{u}$$

$$T = \frac{u\ln 2}{4}\ \text{seconds} \approx 0.173\,u\ \text{seconds}$$
themes: motion of a vehicle with resistance

questions.enonce_markdown: Hence, find the distance travelled by the car in this time.
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Speed as a function of time.** Integrating the equation of part (ii) from $0$ to $t$ (as above) gives $-\ln\dfrac{u - v}{u} = \dfrac{4t}{u}$, so

$$v = u\left(1 - e^{-4t/u}\right)$$

**Distance** in the time $T = \dfrac{u\ln 2}{4}$:

$$s = \int_0^T v\,dt = u\int_0^T\left(1 - e^{-4t/u}\right)dt = u\left[t + \frac{u}{4}e^{-4t/u}\right]_0^T = uT + \frac{u^2}{4}\left(e^{-4T/u} - 1\right)$$

At $t = T$, $e^{-4T/u} = e^{-\ln 2} = \tfrac{1}{2}$, so

$$s = \frac{u^2\ln 2}{4} + \frac{u^2}{4}\left(\frac{1}{2} - 1\right) = \frac{u^2\ln 2}{4} - \frac{u^2}{8} = \frac{u^2\,(2\ln 2 - 1)}{8}\ \text{metres}$$

**$s = \dfrac{u^2(2\ln 2 - 1)}{8} \approx 0.0483\,u^2$ metres.**

(Check with $v\,\dfrac{dv}{dx} = \dfrac{dv}{dt}$: $\displaystyle\int_0^{u/2}\frac{v\,dv}{u - v} = \frac{4}{u}\,s$ gives $u\ln 2 - \dfrac{u}{2} = \dfrac{4s}{u}$, the same result.)
themes: motion of a vehicle with resistance
